identifiers.name: Build
identifiers.why: the image BUILDER is BuildKit, not a selectable engine, so a builder selector would have had exactly one legal value; the runtime config selects the RUN engine instead

identifiers.name: BuildEngine
identifiers.why: the resolved runtime carries the RUN engine; there is no builder to resolve

identifiers.name: build
identifiers.why: the yaml key of the withdrawn builder selector, scoped to the one type it lived on because `build` is still a legal key elsewhere in the contract

identifiers.name: engine.build
identifiers.why: the dotted path the withdrawn builder selector was addressed by

identifiers.name: PodmanJobs
identifiers.why: the knob named the engine it was handed to (`podman build --jobs N`); with one builder there is no second engine to name, so it bounds the STAGES of a single build

identifiers.name: PodmanJobsCap
identifiers.why: the cap on the withdrawn engine-named knob

identifiers.name: podman_jobs
identifiers.why: the authored key of the withdrawn engine-named knob

identifiers.name: podman_jobs_cap
identifiers.why: the authored cap key of the withdrawn engine-named knob

identifiers.name: CHARLY_PODMAN_JOBS
identifiers.why: the environment override of the withdrawn engine-named knob

identifiers.name: CHARLY_BUILD_ENGINE
identifiers.why: the environment override of the withdrawn builder selector

identifiers.name: --podman-jobs
identifiers.why: the command-line flag of the withdrawn engine-named knob
